design.claim: Selection among loop-local VF/IC directives, with LLVM legality and downstream optimization retained; not replacement of the whole vectorizer cost model.
controls: one-nearest-neighbor candidate loss predictor fitted only on discovery
design.discovery_gate: Choose the best constant action including stock and per-case candidate-best actions on discovery block one. Confirm without reselecting on block two. Require at least 5% family-balanced runtime reduction over the fitted constant, gain beyond max(2%, three times maximum paired MAD log ratio), positive direction in at least two discovery families, and distinct code outcomes in at least half discovery cases. Otherwise stop before model calls.
design.maintenance: Count fixed selector rules, learned exemplars, routing parameters, packet features and prompt policy. No human-effort or long-term maintenance claim from this experiment.
design.model_packet: Source numerical features, candidate VF/IC choices and fixed target facts only. No family/case names or timing outcomes. One valid response per provider per identical packet; retain failed attempts and reuse successful responses.
design.name: loop-policy-v1
design.scope: Synthetic single-loop native screening, three fixed trip counts, one CPU. Does not establish whole-program, cross-target or production performance.
design.stop: Fail closed on toolchain, correctness or provenance errors. Gate failure is a valid negative result; do not quietly change controls, corpus or thresholds after timings. A different boundary requires a new design.
design.success: Held-out cascade improvement over the fitted constant, Jev, and nearest-neighbor exceeds max(2%, three times maximum paired MAD log ratio), with positive direction in at least two of three test families for each comparison. Both calibration and held-out escalation rates must be <=25%. Stock comparison is separate. Never force positive routing.
